title: From Persia to Iran: why this civilisation never forgets
ticker: From Airyana Vaeja to the Islamic Republic: the long civilisational arc of Persia and Iran

scenes.title: From Persia to Iran
scenes.say: Empires come and go. Iran has outlasted almost all of them. To see why it still unsettles the world's great powers, start at the very beginning.

scenes.label: kingdoms, bound by language, ritual and belief, not by one ruler
scenes.source: Middle Persian tradition, via Niti Shastra
scenes.say: Middle Persian tradition speaks of as many as 240 kingdoms on the Iranian plateau. They were bound not by one ruler, but by language, ritual and a shared cosmos.
scenes.speak: Middle Persian tradition speaks of as many as two hundred and forty kingdoms on the Iranian plateau. They were bound not by one ruler, but by language, ritual and a shared cosmos.

scenes.title: From Balkh to Pars
scenes.say: Power moved across this world: from Balkh in the east, to Media, to Parthia, and finally to Pars, the province that gave Persia its name. But Persia was never the whole of Iran.

scenes.title: Shahanshah: the King of Kings
scenes.base: Layered sovereignty: echoed in India's Rajadhiraja and Chakravarti
scenes.say: When one kingdom rose, it didn't abolish the others. It ruled over them. That gave the world the Shahanshah, the King of Kings, an idea echoed in India's Rajadhiraja and Chakravarti.

scenes.text: Empire was not annihilation of difference but orchestration of plurality.
scenes.say: In the Iranian imagination, empire was not the annihilation of difference, but the orchestration of plurality.

scenes.title: Persepolis: an imperial voice
scenes.say: In the 6th century BCE, Cyrus built the largest empire yet seen. Alexander conquered it, then adopted its ways. And Persia's heirs were Rome's only true equals.
scenes.speak: In the sixth century BCE, Cyrus built the largest empire yet seen. Alexander conquered it, then adopted its ways. And Persia's heirs were Rome's only true equals.

scenes.role: Iranian historian, on the Arab conquest
scenes.say: Then, the deepest rupture. In the 7th century, the Sasanian empire fell to Arab armies. Language, faith and rulers all changed. One historian called it two centuries of silence.
scenes.speak: Then, the deepest rupture. In the seventh century, the Sasanian empire fell to Arab armies. Language, faith and rulers all changed. One historian called it two centuries of silence.

scenes.title: Even the words remember
scenes.base: Zoroastrians who fled to India kept the old word: Parsi
scenes.say: Arabic has no P sound, so Pars became Fars, and Persian became Farsi. But the Zoroastrians who fled to India kept the older word. They are still called Parsis.

scenes.title: Iran reshaped its rulers
items: Scholars saved and grew Greek science
Seljuk Turks ruled as Persian kings
scenes.say: And Iran didn't die. It reshaped Islam itself. Persians ran the Abbasid Caliphate. Turkic and Mongol conquerors became Persian kings. Again and again, the conqueror was absorbed.

scenes.title: The Safavid synthesis
scenes.base: Faith fused with sovereignty: the blueprint of modern Iran
scenes.say: The Safavids completed the restoration. Twelver Shi'ism became the state faith and a geopolitical firewall against Sunni rivals. Faith fused with sovereignty: the blueprint of modern Iran.

scenes.title: Sovereignty, tested
scenes.say: In the 1800s, Britain and Russia hollowed Iran out. In 1935, Persia became Iran. In 1953, an Anglo-American coup toppled Mossadegh. Then came 1979, and revolution.
scenes.speak: In the eighteen hundreds, Britain and Russia hollowed Iran out. In nineteen thirty-five, Persia became Iran. In nineteen fifty-three, an Anglo-American coup toppled Mossadegh. Then came nineteen seventy-nine, and revolution.

scenes.title: A revolution hardens

photos.caption: Posters of Khamenei and Khomeini at a rally

scenes.say: The revolution hardened into a coercive state, increasingly run by the Revolutionary Guards.

scenes.title: The 'Shia crescent'
scenes.say: Abroad, Iran built allies from Iraq to Lebanon to Yemen, to keep its wars far from home.

scenes.title: Two ancient civilisations
items: Sanskrit and Avestan are linguistic cousins
scenes.say: For India, this is not a distant story. Sanskrit and Avestan are linguistic cousins. Shahanshah meets Chakravarti. And the Parsis carry pre-Islamic Iran in India to this day.

scenes.title: Silence, or renewal?
scenes.say: Now, with the Gulf a tinderbox, Iran faces overwhelming pressure again. History offers two paths: a long silence, or a profound renewal. Because Iran measures history in centuries, not regimes.

scenes.title: Source: Niti Shastra, 'From Persia to Iran'
